criterion: HW H2 inference: our own GPU kernels for the trained network (Vulkan compute), a cooperative-matrix path for the convolutions and a portable scalar path, against the PyTorch forward pass. Elaborates the inference_parity and budget lines of evidence/rr-bounds.json; changes neither.
written: 2026-10-13, before the kernels are written or run
shipped_code: C++ and GLSL in src/rhi/vulkan/ (vk_rrnet*.cpp, shaders/vk_rr_*.comp), no third-party dependency beyond the Vulkan loader the tool already uses. The weights are a flat file exported from our own training (scripts/rr_export.py); PyTorch is used only to produce the comparison outputs.

parity.what: both paths run the full recurrent sequence on every test sequence (their own previous outputs feed the next frame); every pixel of every frame of the remodulated output compared with the PyTorch forward pass run the same way in float32
parity.bound: max absolute difference in linear radiance at most 1e-2 on every pixel of every test frame, for each path
parity.reported: max, 99.99th percentile and mean absolute difference per sequence; the frame and pixel of the max

controls_that_must_fail.weights_perturbed: the scalar path with the first convolution's weights scaled by 1.01 must exceed the parity bound
controls_that_must_fail.fp16_activation_round_trip_everywhere: not a control; reported only if run

budget: as rr-bounds.json: the cooperative-matrix path at 1920 x 1080 output on the RTX 4090, median of 500 frames after 50 warm-up, at most 2.0 ms, timed with GPU timestamps around the whole network including the glue kernels; the timing protocol of PLAN.md (three runs with GPU snapshots) applies; the scalar path is timed and reported, not bounded
adapters: parity of the scalar path on SwiftShader locally; both paths on the RTX 4090 only under D:/gpu.lock.d, in holds of minutes between MMBU runs
does_not_prove: Image quality (that is rr-bounds.json's comparison); speed on other GPUs; that a fused or fp16-activation design would not be faster.
